invariants.name: An admitted proof has a manifest base that is an ancestor of the diff target
A proof with a base ref reads its diff from the merge base

carrier.contract: Each arrow reads Git through historyGit and returns a Result. A refusal names the commits, and no arrow writes a file.

category.equality: Two base pairs are equal when their manifest and diff commits are equal. Two refusals are equal when their text is equal.

abstraction.hides: The Git reads of the merge base, the ancestry test that ignores replace objects and grafts, and the merge base view of each ratified record.
callersKnow: The diff base is the merge base of the ref and HEAD, or the manifest base when no ref is given.
A manifest base that is not an ancestor of the diff target stops, and the stop names both commits.
Ratification history stays at the manifest base.
Each CI run of scripts/check-proof.ts passes a base.
abstraction.deletionTest: Deleting the base paragraphs leaves the README and the runbooks with the old rule that the manifest base must equal the base ref. Deleting proofBase puts the ancestor rule into check proof and check ci-pins, so the two commands can drift apart.

alternatives.name: Keep the long opening of the README
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A newcomer cannot read six detailed bullets in 20 seconds, and each detail repeats a later section.

alternatives.name: Copy the full base rule into each doc
alternatives.rejectedBecause: The proof contract is the one home of the rule, so each other doc states the rule in short and links to it.

alternatives.name: Keep the state counts of the repository proof in the README
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Each new manifest changes the model and its counts, so the README goes stale at the next PR.

omitted: Git itself, its object store and the merge base algorithm are abstracted to one base observation for each run.
The CI event payload and the remote refs of the checkout are taken as true.
The earlier authority, landing, evidence and Result law parts of the model stay as they were.

bounds: One base observation for each run from 48 cases: four relations, a ref or none, two diff bases, two history views and an authority move that needs a ref.
The authority cases, five validation stages and the bounded positive, negative, restored and freshness results of the earlier model.
Finite Result laws use two values, two errors and all total functions between them.

negative.defect: Dropping the base relation guard admits a manifest base that is not an ancestor of the merge base, so the scope check can miss paths of the PR.

limits: The finite model takes the Git ancestry, diff and history observations as true. It does not model Git.
The model does not check the words of the docs. Review and the STE, chart, budget and drift gates examine them.
The skill, agent, rules, handler and check counts in the README are observations of the tree at this commit.
Exact-head CI, review and every ordinary gate stay required.
